description: Uniform kameo actor progress and lifecycle, registry mailboxes, and connection and transport health; failing asks are not errors in the uniform metrics, actor="connection" covers binding commands only, stanza turns use waddle.connection_actor.turn.duration, and message types are available through the actor.handle_message span's message attribute in Tempo rather than metric attributes.

panels.description: Falling handled throughput or rising waits and handler occupancy indicate actors may be unable to keep up with incoming work.
panels.title: All actors
Handled messages per second by actor
panels.description: A handled-message rate that stops despite demand indicates a stuck actor, whose waiting messages produce no queue-wait observations until they reach a handler.

panels.title: Queue wait p50 and p99 by actor
panels.description: High queue-wait percentiles indicate delays before handling among messages that reach a handler, including sender backpressure and on_start for startup-buffered messages.

panels.title: Handler duration p50 and p99 by actor
panels.description: High handler-duration percentiles indicate long actor occupancy; delegated reply work is excluded, so use xmpp.actor.mailbox.latency for room registry end-to-end latency.

panels.title: Actor busy fraction by actor
panels.description: A busy fraction near 1 (100%) means that single-instance actor is saturated on that pod; actors with many instances per pod are left out, and delegated reply work is excluded.
Unexpected churn, panicked stops, or dead actors indicate unstable actor lifecycles.
panels.title: Lifecycle
Starts and stops per second by actor
panels.description: Sustained starts and stops beyond expected workload churn indicate unstable actors; starts follow successful on_start and stops count started actors leaving their message loop.

panels.title: Panicked stops by actor (interval increase)
panels.description: Any panicked stops in the rate interval indicate a lifecycle hook or handler panicked or returned a fatal error.

panels.title: Live actors estimate by actor
panels.description: An unexplained rise or fall can indicate retained actors or actor loss, but this starts-minus-stops estimate resets per pod restart and may be absent until a stop series exists.

targets.expr: sum by (actor) (waddle_actor_started_total) - (sum by (actor) (waddle_actor_stopped_total) or 0 * sum by (actor) (waddle_actor_started_total))

panels.title: Dead actors detected by actor and reason
panels.description: A nonzero detection rate means a registry found dead actors and removed them without respawning, so callers can fail.

panels.title: User actors reaped
panels.description: An unexpected reaping rate relative to session churn can indicate excessive user actor turnover, while normal reaping removes empty user actors.
Growing registry mailbox depth, request latency, drops, or timeouts indicate backpressure or stalled request completion.
panels.title: Registry mailboxes
Mailbox depth by actor, class and capacity
panels.description: Sustained mailbox depth near max_capacity indicates registry backpressure and a risk of dropped requests.

panels.title: Mailbox request latency p50 and p99
panels.description: High end-to-end request latency percentiles indicate slow registry replies, including delegated reply work excluded from uniform handler duration.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.50, sum by (le, actor, operation, class) (rate(xmpp_actor_mailbox_latency_milliseconds_bucket[$__rate_interval])))
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, actor, operation, class) (rate(xmpp_actor_mailbox_latency_milliseconds_bucket[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Dropped requests by actor, operation, class and reason
panels.description: A rising dropped-request rate indicates registry requests lost to backpressure or actor shutdown for the shown reasons.

panels.title: Request timeouts by actor, operation and class
panels.description: A rising timeout rate indicates registry requests exceeded their mailbox or reply deadline.
Long connection turns, mailbox rejections, or unexpected retirements and pump exits indicate impaired connection progress.
panels.title: Connection actor and transport
Connection turn duration p50 and p99 by event
panels.description: High turn-duration percentiles indicate slow connection stanza turns that are not covered by the uniform actor="connection" binding-command metrics.

panels.title: Connection mailbox rejections by lane and reason
panels.description: A rising rejection rate indicates connection mailbox admission is failing for the shown lane and reason.

panels.title: Connection actor retirements by cause
panels.description: Unexpected retirement causes or a surge beyond normal connection churn indicate connection actors are losing progress or shutting down abnormally.

panels.title: Transport pump exits by pump and cause
panels.description: Unexpected pump exit causes or a surge beyond normal disconnects indicate transport read or write failures.

panels.title: Transport custodian retirements by cause
panels.description: Unexpected custodian retirement causes or a surge beyond normal disconnects indicate sockets and their pumps are being retired abnormally.
